bullets.title: Oil drops on Iran Hormuz reopening signals, then rebounds on denial
bullets.body: Brent fell below $100/bbl and WTI dropped ~$2 to ~$90 on reports Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 7 days if the US lifts its port blockade; Iran's Fars news agency subsequently denied the Kyodo/Reuters reports. Saudi Arabia separately restarted its East-West pipeline and prepared to resume Yanbu crude exports, adding further supply relief. BofA raised its H2 2026 Brent forecast to $95 from $83 on persistent Hormuz disruptions running 4-8mb/d below pre-war levels.

bullets.title: US diesel hits record $6.53/gal; oil shock threatens to disable Fed policy response
bullets.body: US diesel prices reached a record $6.527/gallon, up from $3.69 a year ago, driven by restricted Russian exports and Hormuz disruptions. Hedgeye warns the WTI shock (~+$20 since late August, futures in severe backwardation) is hitting headline CPI immediately — September CPI Nowcast already +27bps vs August — a setup historically seen before the 1990 Kuwait invasion, 2008 GFC, and 2022 Ukraine invasion. Prior oil shocks arrived into downturns already underway and disabled policy response.

bullets.title: Fed hiking into slowdown; 10s/2s curve compresses to ~19bps, CPI nowcast 3.67%
bullets.body: The Fed hiked 25bps last week with three more hikes expected by April 2027; Hedgeye's inflation nowcast rose to 3.67% y/y vs 3.40% reported CPI, supporting higher-for-longer yields. The 10s/2s curve compressed to ~19bps, which Hedgeye calls the biggest macro problem since early 2022. Morgan Stanley expects two additional hikes to 4.25%-4.50%, held through end of 2027; Chicago Fed's Goolsbee described the employment-vs-inflation tradeoff as 'painful' amid the stagflationary shock.

bullets.title: S&P breadth deteriorating despite index strength; market concentrated in ~20 names
bullets.body: Market breadth continues to deteriorate across Consumer Discretionary, Tech, and Financials even as the S&P held near highs, with signal rotation turning defensive per Hedgeye. The S&P has gone 36 sessions without a -1% decline — longest in nearly a year — but three-quarters of the index's 93% gain since ChatGPT's release came from just 20 companies, with NVDA accounting for ~16%. High Beta Momentum longs show the largest divergence between YTD and QTD performance.

bullets.title: Post-FOMC factor rotation: momentum/growth surge, defensives/value fade
bullets.body: A quant strategy note flags the MIRC shifted from Risk Averse to Broad Selloff post-FOMC, with Momentum, Growth, and Risk-on factors rebounding sharply while Risk-off and Value weakened. Investors rotated into Early Cyclicals, particularly Technology, over Deep Cyclicals. AI-driven correlation changes put Momentum/Growth at the 90th percentile correlation with Risk-on/Earnings Turbulence — a structural shift from historical patterns. The outlook favors Growth Continuation regime as implied volatility declines.

bullets.title: S&P bull case requires AI story intact, 10-yr below 5%, WTI below $100 — all currently check
bullets.body: OpCo Industrials identifies three conditions for the S&P to move higher: AI narrative intact, 10-year Treasury yield below 5%, and WTI below $100. All three currently hold, with SPX breaking above 7656 triggering a bullish trade signal per Hedgeye. Gamma flipped positive as SPX reclaimed its key trade level. MS CIO Wilson maintains bull market thesis on quality stocks, strong earnings, and price momentum.

bullets.title: AI capex driving ~50% of S&P EPS growth in 2026, but depreciation drag looms in 2027
bullets.body: Goldman forecasts AI accounts for nearly 50% of S&P 500 earnings growth this year, but contribution is expected to moderate as hyperscaler capex slows from a current ~$800B run rate. A depreciation drag of ~5 percentage points on 2027 earnings could offset nearly half of the capex benefit. Taiwan export orders hit a record $104B in August (+71.4% y/y), with US orders reaching $42B (+88.9%), confirming AI boom — but slowing actual export growth raises double-ordering risk.

bullets.title: Data center buildout faces multi-state regulatory pushback; nuclear power filling gap
bullets.body: Texas Gov. Abbott halted all state-issued data center environmental permits pending a grid/water audit; LA County halted new data center developments; OpenAI's Georgia project faces litigation. On the supply side, Google agreed to fund ~96MW of nuclear capacity increases at two Georgia plants, and NVDA doubled its cumulative investment in SoftBank-backed SB Energy to $3B ahead of IPO. SoftBank's ~$11B junk bond offering for OpenAI investments drew ~$20B early demand.

bullets.title: Section 301 tariff legal challenge Sept 30 could trigger ~$100B in refunds
bullets.body: New Section 301 tariffs (10-12.5%) covering 99% of US imports face a Court of International Trade challenge on Sept 30; challengers argue global application exceeds statutory authority. If invalidated — analogous to IEEPA precedent where ~$170B in refunds were generated ~10 months post-imposition — roughly $100B in refunds could flow to importers. Atlanta Fed survey found ~25% of executives are already seeking or have received tariff refunds.

bullets.title: Richmond Fed manufacturing softens in September; ISM tracking 54.5% vs 55.0% consensus
bullets.body: The Richmond Fed manufacturing index fell 6 points to -2.0% in September (ISM-equivalent to 51.6%), with new orders slipping below zero and capex plans declining. Morgan Stanley's tracking puts the September ISM at 53.9 vs 54.6 in August. Three regional surveys combined point to a 54.5% ISM print vs the 55.0% consensus. One positive offset: headcount jumped to a 20-month high, though prices paid rose while prices received were flat, compressing margins.

bullets.title: Chicago Fed CFNAI cooled to -0.04 in August; Goolsbee flags 'painful' stagflation tradeoff
bullets.body: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index slipped to -0.04 in August from +0.08 prior (revised up from -0.08), with only 39 of 85 indicators positive. The 3-month moving average edged back into positive territory at +0.01. Goolsbee explicitly described the current environment as a 'painful trade-off' between employment and inflation, with restrictive rates expected to weaken labor markets.

bullets.title: Banks sold on positioning unwind, not AI disruption; L/S ratio at 82nd percentile
bullets.body: JPM sales desk attributes aggressive bank selling to positioning unwind, not fundamental repricing. Large cap banks (C, MS, GS, USB) are dominating volume while regionals and boutiques outperform — a 'classic positioning unwind signature.' The L/S ratio remained elevated at the 82nd percentile at week-start despite 20 days of net selling, implying substantial further unwind risk. JPM argues AI capex requirements represent opportunity for banks, not risk.

bullets.title: Agentic commerce disruption basket down 12%; Amazon blocks Meta Muse as threat validates
bullets.body: META is +20% since Muse's 9/8 launch while an agentic commerce disruption basket of threatened aggregators is down 12%. Amazon cut off Meta's Muse agent from its marketplace citing privacy/security risks — interpreted as validation of the agentic threat to its retail media model ($68B ads revenue vs. $34B e-commerce profit). The note draws an analogy to GLP-1 disruption shorts that fell 50-70% over a 3-year holding period, and argues agentic commerce is in the 'first inning.'

bullets.title: Insurance/fintech sector hit by agentic AI disintermediation fears; EVER -13%
bullets.body: Multiple insurance and fintech names (EVER -13.2%, GSHD, QNST, ALL, LPLA) declined on unusual volume amid growing concern that agentic AI agents — specifically Meta's Muse — could disintermediate trust-based financial service models. StreetAccount flagged 196% of average 30-day volume in EVER with no company-specific news. JPM's bank note counters that AI can't disintermediate trust-based banking.

bullets.title: Kalshi odds shift: 61% Dems retake Senate, 91% Dems take House in November
bullets.body: Prediction market Kalshi now assigns 61% probability to Democrats regaining Senate control (Republicans currently hold 53-47) and 91% probability to Democrats taking the House (Republicans hold 218-214). The shift has potential implications for regulatory and fiscal policy into 2027.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit: Yardeni sees trade truce extension only; Xi to press on Taiwan arms sales
bullets.body: Yardeni Research expects no 'grand bargain' from the Trump-Xi meeting, only a trade truce extension. Separately, Xi is expected to press Trump to halt US arms sales to Taiwan, including already-ordered weapons. Shanghai stocks closed up only +0.06% overnight despite bullish media framing of the summit talks.

bullets.title: Euro area consumer confidence -1pt in Sept; JPM forecasts 1.25% annualized consumption growth in 3Q
bullets.body: The European Commission flash consumer confidence indicator fell 1 point in September as higher energy prices pressure household budgets. JPM's forecast stands at 1.25% annualized consumption growth in 3Q26, a modest acceleration from 0.9% in 1H26, sitting between its bridge model (0.7%) and DFM nowcast (2.0%). Downside risks include weak retail sales and potential payback from strong 2Q durables spending.

bullets.title: Office CMBS delinquency hits 12%, above post-GFC record; apartment CLOs stressed
bullets.body: US office CMBS delinquency reached 12% in August/September 2026, surpassing post-GFC 2008 levels. Apartment CLO distress jumped in August, with 2021 vintages — originated before rate hikes — facing significantly higher stress. Fed hiking into a supply-side energy shock rather than demand excess risks deepening housing contraction, per Citi real estate commentary.

bullets.title: Small caps face near-term headwinds but offer +30% upside if AI closes margin gap
bullets.body: Large caps are expected to grow earnings ~2x small caps over the next 12 months, driven by faster AI adoption — small cap AI users currently show worse TTM and NTM margins than non-AI users. However, small cap 2-year EPS CAGR (+22.4%) exceeds large caps (+20.9%), and for every 1pp of margin growth, small cap fair value increases ~10%. If small caps close the 1.7pp margin gap and ERP re-rates to the historical midpoint, upside to fair value is +30%. Relief is contingent on oil moving significantly lower.

bullets.title: Hedgeye repositions: long energy, mega-cap tech (AAPL/MSFT/META), PFIX; short utilities, industrials, small caps
bullets.body: Keith McCullough added energy (XLE) and bond volatility (PFIX) to asset allocation after buying WTI at $87 with a $90.17-108.16 risk range. He is long AAPL, MSFT, META as signal-strength stocks and Software (IGV) over the Nasdaq composite. He is short Utilities (XLU), Industrials (XLI), Russell 2000, Switzerland, and Germany. Gold was reduced below minimum position, silver sold, and gold miners exited.
